CHEN AND THOMAS PETERNELL INTRODUCTION Given a line bundle \(L\) on a projective manifold \(X\), the Nakai-Moishezon criterion says that \(L\) is ample if and only if \[ L^s \cdot Y > 0 \] for all irreducible subvarieties \(Y \subset X\) of dimension \(s \le \dim Y\). Examples show that it is not sufficient to assume that \(L \cdot C > 0\) for all curves; line bundles with this property are called strictly nef. If however \(K_X\) is strictly nef, then standard conjectures predict that \(K_X\) is already ample; this is proved in dimension up to 3 (Kawamata, Miyaoka, see e.g. [Ko92]). If \(\dim X = 3\) and \(-K_X\) is strictly nef, then Serrano [Se95] showed that \(-K_X\) is ample, i.e. \(X\) is a Fano threefold. This lead him to set up the following 0.1. Conjecture. Let \(X\) be a projective manifold of dimension \(n\) and \(L\) a strictly nef line bundle on \(X\). Then \(K_X + tL\) is ample for any real \(t > n + 1\). {mainconj} A different view to this conjecture is as follows. -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- algebraic conjecture of M. Strictly nef divisors, Serrano’s conjecture, Ampleness conjecture, Campana– Peternell’s conjecture. 1 2 HAIDONG LIU There are three important special cases of the log version of Serrano’s conjecture: (i) K X is numerically trivial; (ii)L=−K X is strictly nef; (iii)L=K X is strictly nef. We pay attention to the ﬁrst two cases in this paper. 1.1. The case K X≡0.In this case, the log version of Serrano’s conjecture is also called ampleness conjecture when ∆ = 0: Conjecture 1.2 (Ampleness conjecture).Let X be a projective log canonical variety with numerically trivial canonical divisor. Then, any strictly nef Q-Cartier divisors on X are ample. As the smooth case [20, Conjecture 1.1], Conjecture 1.2 is also a special case of the semi- (see Deﬁnition 2.2). In this case, we obtain some partial results: Theorem 1.4 (Theorems 3.10 and 3.14).Let X be a Q-factorial canonical Calabi–Yau threefold and L be a strictly nef Q-Cartier divisor on X. (1) if ν(X, L) = 2, then H p(X, Ω[q] X(mL)) = 0 for all p, q ≥0 and m≫1; (2) if ν(X, L) = 1 and X admits a ﬁbration f:X→S, then f is an equiv-dimensional elliptic ﬁbration and S is a log terminal Fano surface with ρ(S) = 1. In the proofs of above theorems, we use the inductive strategy as in [4,19,20,29] and the references therein. Note that in this inductive strategy, the log version of the ampleness conjecture with a nonzero boundary ∆plays an important role, which is established in dimension 3 (see Subsection 2.4 and Proposition 3.6). 1.2. The case L=−K X is strictly nef. In this case, the log version of Serrano’s conjecture is also a singular version of Campana–Peternell’s conjecture when ∆ = 0: Conjecture 1.5 (Log version of Campana–Peternell’s conjecture).Let X be a projective log canonical variety such that −K X is strictly nef. Then, −K X is ample. The smooth version of Campana–Peternell’s conjecture has been conﬁrmed in dimension 2 by Maeda [23] and in dimension 3 by Serrano [29]. RATIONAL CURVES & STRICTLY NEF DIVISORS ON CYS 1595 In [Ser95], Serrano showed that Conjecture 5.1 holds in dimension 2, and that in dimension 3 the only unknown cases are the following two: (i) \(X\) is a Calabi–Yau threefold and \(c_2(X)\cdot D = 0\), and (ii) \(\kappa(K_X) = -\infty\), and either the irregularity \(q(X)\le 1\) or else \(q(X)=2\) and \(\chi(\mathcal{O}_X)=0\). A decade later, Campana–Chen–Peternell [CCP08] ruled out the latter case and proved some partial results for projective manifolds of dimension higher than 3. When \(X\) is a Calabi–Yau threefold and \(D\) is a strictly nef divisor, by Lemma 2.2, we can assume that \(\kappa(D)=-\infty\) and \(c_2(X)\cdot D=0\), which in turn implies that \(D^3=0\) and \(1\le \nu(D)\le 2\). The results proven in the previous sections allow us to prove that Serrano’s conjecture holds on a Calabi–Yau threefold if we assume that the numerical dimension \(\nu(D)\) of the strictly nef divisor \(D\) is \(\ne 1\), when \(c_3(X)\ne 0\).
